9238989e4a.q: What are five different ways to measure success in farm marketing beyond revenue targets?
9238989e4a.a: Corinna Bench describes having a menu of ways to define success: changing your vantage point to see the same circumstances differently. Rather than looking at a single metric like revenue, you can evaluate whether you tried something new, learned along the way, followed through on something you'd been avoiding, or achieved progress on other business metrics. The key is recognizing that the facts don't change—three people attended the workshop, the promotion made $800—but the meaning you assign to those facts is often a choice, and you can practice looking at situations from different angles to discover success moments you hadn't considered.

f744c7d28e.q: How should farmers define success metrics before launching Black Friday or holiday promotions?
f744c7d28e.a: Corinna Bench recommends deciding how to define success before you launch a promotion, not after looking at a single sales number. She coaches Farm Marketing School members not to wake up Monday morning and label an entire promotion a failure because they didn't hit one revenue target. Instead, identify multiple success markers in advance—such as customer acquisition, email open rates, learning outcomes, or following through on implementation—so you have several ways to celebrate what actually happened rather than fixating on one unmet goal.

c468abdc16.q: What is the vantage point metaphor Corinna Bench uses to explain changing perspectives on marketing results?
c468abdc16.a: Corinna Bench tells a story about hiking Mount Muskoka in Colorado Springs with her husband. After reaching the summit and placing a rock to mark a personal milestone, she walked another 300-400 feet along the ridgeline and noticed the same city looked different from that new vantage point—she could see more of it, though nothing about Colorado Springs itself had changed. She uses this metaphor to explain that when evaluating marketing results, the facts stay the same but your perspective changes what you see, allowing you to discover success that was there all along.
